:::{#hero-heading}

I'm a PhD student in Psychology at the [University of Toronto](https://www.psych.utoronto.ca/graduate), supervised by [Dr. Anthony Ruocco](https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/psych/person/anthony-c-ruocco) in the [Clinical Neurosciences Laboratory](clinicalneurosciences.ca).

My research is focused on examining **psychological measurement** (AKA *psychometrics*) through a critical lens and through traditional approaches, with respect to **mental health** and **personality** attributes. I'm interested in evaluating existing psychological measurement procedures and assumptions, clarifying the mechanisms involved in such measurement, and exploring potential improvements. Questions include:

- What exactly are we measuring with psychological scales and how? 
- How should we measure psychological attributes?
- What utility can psychological measurement provide?

I'm also interested in teaching and have experience teaching statistics as a Course Instructor in the University of Toronto's [Clinical Psychology](https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/psych/clinical-psychology) program, as well as experience providing statistical consulting to researchers.

You can read more about my research and teaching in the other pages of my website. Feel free to contact me through email and thanks for stopping by! 

:::
